In this study, we evaluate the impact of the introduction of linked block orders on market clearing quantities, social welfare, and the earnings of generators by using a multi-agent simulation of a wholesale power exchange. To investigate whether the impact is due to linked block orders or to supply and demand quantities, simulations are performed by varying the quantity demanded. Numerical calculations show that regardless of the quantity demanded, considering linked block orders leads to higher market clearing prices and an increase in producer surplus.

articleTitle: Optimisation of Transient Stability for Integration of Offshore Oil Rigs with Offshore Wind
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: In the developments of offshore oil and gas rigs, the adoption of IEC standards 61892-1 is used to ensure that voltage and frequency deviation are within ranges for power stability during oil and gas production. Dynamic load demand and stochastic wind may lead to large deviations in voltage and frequency, fail to meet IEC standards 61892-1. Hence, a methodology of feed forward control (FFC) is developed in electrical transient analyser program (ETAP) with simulation results generated in this promising results. The integration of wind turbine generation (WTG) with oil and gas (O&G) rigs and battery energy storage system (BESS) has shown an improvement in power quality with optimal transient stability. This proposed method can be achieved when there is a need to consider a realistic wind profile which is of stochastic wind speed and dynamic loads from the offshore O&G rigs.

articleTitle: Sliding Mode Observer based FCS-MPC Control of Voltage Source Inverter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This paper introduces a Sliding Mode Observer (SMO) based Finite Control Set Model Predictive Control (FCSMPC) strategy. A digital model of the system, implemented in Matlab/Simulink, is utilized to verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The simulation results, encompassing both steady-state and dynamic analyses, are discussed and benchmarked against traditional FCS-MPC. The results highlight improved total harmonic distortion (THD) values, superior dynamic response, and more stable performance when integrating SMO into the FCS-MPC methodology.

articleTitle: Neural Network Based Fault Location in Power Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Locating the fault in the power distribution system is a tedious process that involves manually searching along the line. While some methods rely on complete system parameters or centralized data processing, it has become difficult due to the bidirectional power flow in the active distribution system. This paper proposes a framework consisting of three steps: detecting, classifying, and locating the fault in the active distribution system. The proposed method reduces the search area by using the sending-end sample value of the line current. It can be implemented in a distributed form without knowledge of system parameters using pole-mounted data recording meters and relaying the approximate fault location and type to the control center. In the first step, the fault is detected using an isolation forest. Then, the fault is classified by the support vector machine, and finally, the fault is located using an adaptive weight convolutional neural network (CNN). The CNN weights are modified according to fault type information that uses time-frequency information extracted by a continuous wavelet transform (CWT). The proposed framework is tested using an IEEE 13-node test feeder with a solar photovoltaic system. Different training parameters for the CNN are also tested to analyze the proposed framework

articleTitle: Evaluating the Financial Viability of Vehicle-to-Grid for Autonomous Electric Ride-Hailing Fleets
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Flexibility is a key requirement for future electricity markets. While both smart charging and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology have emerged as critical elements to fulfill this need, V2G adoption lags behind. Fleets of autonomous electric vehicles (AEVs) in the ride-hailing industry offer new prospects for the adoption of V2G, but an evaluation of the economic viability remains imperative. We propose a deep reinforcement learning algorithm for an operator of a ride-hailing fleet of V2G-enabled AEVs, seeking profit-maximizing strategies for fleet (dis)charging based on passenger demand and real market prices. By empirically evaluating our algorithm using data from ride-hailing operations in Manhattan, we find that it leads to only a marginal increase in profits compared to smart charging, suggesting the need for additional incentives to encourage V2G adoption. Our findings offer insights into the potential of V2G for ride-hailing and highlight the challenges and opportunities for policymakers to consider.

articleTitle: Innovating the way out of the energy crisis: Commercialization pathways of home energy management user-innovations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: User innovations can have a significant impact on new and rapidly evolving markets of technologies, such as home energy management systems (HEMS), which are predicted to grow significantly in the near future. This study describes user innovators’ motivations, the user innovations and their scalability potential, and clarifies the business model design aspects that come across when commercializing them. The data for this research was collected with semi-structured interviews with individual users and solution providers in Finland during the energy crisis in 20222023.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of Northern Regional Transmission System of India: Critical Analysis for Grid Resilience
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The resilience of electricity grids is of utmost importance to ensure uninterrupted electricity supply and sustain the functionality of critical infrastructure and essential services. This paper presents a comprehensive evaluation of the resilience of the Northern Regional Transmission Grid of India for the year 2022. The study assesses the grid’s ability to withstand and recover from various challenges, including extreme weather events, equipment failures, overloading. The evaluation of northern grid resilience involves the analysis of multiple factors, including frequency of outages, response time to disruptions, impact of outages and voltage control through reactor operations and AC line opening. To conduct the assessment, historical outage records, and other related data have been utilized. The study underscores the importance of investing in robust grid infrastructure, network upgrades, proactive maintenance practices, and modernization initiatives, advanced technologies to strengthen the resilience of power grids and ensure uninterrupted transfer of power.

Author Keywords: Extra High Voltage AC (EHV AC) Transmission Line

articleTitle: Correction Method of Baseline Load Estimation Result Based on the Identification and Evaluation of the Rebound Effect
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: As the basis for incentive-based demand response (DR) settlement, accurate customer baseline load (CBL) estimates are critical. However, the existence of the rebound effect will cause users to rebound their load after participating in incentive demand response events. This phenomenon will change the user’s electricity consumption pattern, and if the additional factors introduced by the rebound effect are not considered, estimating CBL using traditional methods will have significant bias. Therefore, this paper proposes a method for the identification and comprehensive evaluation of the rebound effect. After that, a neural network is built to get the mapping relationship between rebound effect evaluation index and the CBL deviation. Finally, a way of getting the deviation of the CBL result caused by RE is proposed. In order to correct the CBL, the paper first uses wavelet decomposition to identify the rebound effect, and then, this paper established the comprehensive evaluation index system to comprehensively evaluates the rebound effect. Finally, the BP neural network is selected to correct the deviation of the baseline load estimation result caused by the rebound effect. Simulation experiments show that this method can correct the deviation of baseline load estimation results caused by rebound effect.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing EV Adoption: Enhancing User Participation through SOC Strategies Incorporating Degradation-Dependent Economic Model for Battery Swapping Stations
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: The slow deployment of charging infrastructure and weak power grid are major barriers to the widespread adoption of electric vehicles (EVs), particularly in developing countries. Battery swapping stations have emerged as a potential solution to accelerate transport electrification by offering a convenient, cost-effective, and sustainable way to recharge EVs. In this model, battery swapping station owners have invested in setting up the stations and want to increase user participation to recover their investment and make the business profitable. To achieve this, swapping stations can introduce different categories of EV users, such as daily earners, daily commuters, and inter-city travelers, and provide them with different plans tailored to their needs. In this paper, we propose a degradation-dependent economic model to extend battery cycle life and reduce investment costs for the station owner, while ensuring a fair and sustainable swapping cost for the users. We suggest state-of-charge strategies for each category of EV users and use the degradation model to calculate deterioration and add a degradation penalty component to create a fair swapping cost. We propose two models (linear and exponential) for the degradation penalty and conclude that daily earners and commuters should be penalized linearly, while inter-city travelers should be penalized exponentially. Our results demonstrate that introducing different plans tailored to the needs of different categories of EV users and applying the degradation-dependent economic model can increase user participation in battery swapping stations and help overcome the challenges of charging infrastructure and grid limitations. This can contribute to the wider adoption of EVs and the transition to a more sustainable transportation system.

Author Keywords: Increasing EV adoption Battery Swapping Station

articleTitle: Planning and Management of Distributed Energy Resources for Achieving the Target Renewable Energy Rate in Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Distributed energy resources (DERs) such as photovoltaics (PV) and battery energy storage system (BESS) are effective for improving the target renewable energy (RE) rate in a region. Furthermore, it is expected that distribution system operators (DSOs) will promote their installation in the future. However, it is not enough for DSOs to simply install large-capacity PV and BESS. They need to determine these capacities by taking into account the cost reduction of equipment and the constraints on grid operation. In this paper, we propose a DER installation capacity optimization method based on linear programming using annual data and a layout method from the operator’s perspective. This method determines the capacity of DERs based on the target RE utilization rate in a controlled area of a distribution system. Furthermore, we report the results of an analysis of power flow when the DER is introduced. Moreover, we estimate the actual required capacity of DERs for a real 2-feeder distribution system model. In addition, power flow calculations are performed for a typical day where that amount of DERs were installed. The results were evaluated in terms of grid voltage, thermal capacity of line, and distribution losses, and the necessary controls were discussed.

articleTitle: Grid Congestion Management using Grouping of Renewable Energies based on Sensitivity Analysis and Grid Congestion Amount of Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: This study proposes an output curtailment method for determining the output curtailment of renewable energy sources (REs) to mitigate grid congestion in transmission systems with a significant influx of REs. To manage congestion, minimizing the total REs output curtailment while avoiding the concentrated output curtailment on a specific RE is crucial. As a means of identifying effective curtailment targets for congestion mitigation, sensitivity analysis is being used for quantifying the congestion mitigation effect with curtailment. Furthermore, equality in output curtailment can be ensured by grouping REs of similar sensitivity and uniformly curtailing each group. Minimizing the curtailment of REs under the grouping-based approach requires forming a group of REs that is sensitive to frequently congested lines, considering the tendency of congestion occurrence in the whole grid. Consequently, this study proposes a method for determining the output curtailment rate of REs using grouping based on weighted sensitivity, considering the sensitivity of each RE and grid congestion. The effectiveness of the proposed method was evaluated by numerical simulation of congestion management over one year on a grid in the northern area of the Tohoku region in Japan. The results indicated that the proposed method was superior in terms of total REs curtailment and equality compared to the comparison method that does not consider the grid congestion amount.

articleTitle: Leveraging Digital Twins and Demand Side Recommender Chatbot for Optimizing Smart Grid Energy Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Electricity consumers often face the challenge of selecting an optimal plan for saving energy. Strategic energy management and monitoring plays a key role in overcoming these challenges. Developments around Industry 5.0 powered smart grid proffers adequate solutions which allows end-consumers to monitor their energy performance towards effecting demand side recommendation services. Specific problems where end-users are likely to ignore recommended advice exists, thereby contributing to widening ‘knowledge-action gap’. An ensemble of hybrid digital twins (DT) asset modelling based on ordinary differential equation (ODE) physics engine and data driven recurrent neural network (RNN) prediction approach alongside PageRank based asset behavior scoring algorithm deployed for demand side recommender and generative pre-trained transformers (GPT) based conversational chatbot technology show effectiveness in engaging and extending end-consumers interests in recommended advice. The novelty of the study lies in extending current scope of demand side recommender scheme via conversational chatbot interface for DT of electricity grid assets that better engage and monitors end-user’s energy behavior while offering appropriate energy efficiency advice towards achieving energy conservation goals of smart grid consumers. Extensive experiments, including evaluation of end-user studies, revealed the effectiveness of proposed approach in terms of improved recommendation quality and user engagement towards net electricity demand reduction.

articleTitle: Day-ahead Demand Response Potential Forecasting Model Based on BILSTM for Load Aggregators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: With the continuous development of social economy, the exhibition of stable, continuous and efficient power supply has become the focus of the global energy field. However, the traditional load aggregator model can not deal with irregular time series data and variable-length series flexibly, which makes the traditional model face certain difficulties in adapting to practical application scenarios. Therefore, considering the real-time and efficiency of the model, a demand response (DR) potential prediction model based on bidirectional long-term and short-term memory network (BiLSTM) is proposed. Firstly, customers are divided into different types according to their willingness to reduce economic costs and respond, and then a Home Energy Management System (HEMS) model considering electricity price incentives is constructed. Secondly, the Light gradient boosting machine (LightGBM) model is used to rank several influencing features according to their importance, which reduces the redundancy of input features. Finally, on the basis of selecting features, BILSTM model is introduced to predict the DR potential of load aggregators (Las). The results of the simulation-based experimentation unequivocally demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Municipalities’ ecosystem roles in different energy communities
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Municipalities are in a crucial position regarding initiating and implementing energy communities. Existing literature acknowledges their role but focuses on production-based energy cooperatives, and there is a need for a more comprehensive view of potential ecosystem roles. This study uses the ecosystem approach to present an overview of different energy communities and municipalities’ roles in them. Mostly, the municipalities have a supportive and reactive role, but especially in more complex settings like microgrids, they also can have a proactive ecosystem leadership role in coordinating and facilitating energy communities.

articleTitle: An Investigative Study for the Commercialization of Anion Exchange Membrane-based Unitized Regenerative Fuel Cell
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Renewable energy storage in the form of hydrogen is favored because vast quantities of energy can be stored for both short and long periods of time, and hydrogen can be decoupled from demand. Low-temperature water electrolysis is a feasible method for storing seasonal energy in the form of hydrogen over an extended period of time. In addition, a fuel cell aids in the conversion of hydrogen to electricity. When the electrolyzer and the fuel cell units are combined, a discrete regenerative fuel cell is formed. A combination of the electrolyzer and fuel cell processes in one device is referred to as a unitized regenerative fuel cell. When renewable electricity is available, the unitized regenerative fuel cell serves as a storage facility for energy by splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen. When wind or solar resources are not available or when electricity is required, the hydrogen and oxygen are then recombined to produce water, thereby providing electricity to the grid. The unitized regenerative fuel cell is currently the most cost effective long-term seasonal energy storage solution available. The primary advantage of unitized regenerative fuel cells is the reduced capex associated with the consolidation of two electrolyzer and fuel cell stacks into one. The anion exchange membrane-based unitized regenerative fuel cell is a promising option for large-scale renewable energy storage and hydrogen generation. It is concluded with mention of some challenges and then suggestions for potential actions relevant to the development of long-lasting anion exchange membrane-based unitized regenerative fuel cells.

articleTitle: Introducing Digitalisation to Component Risk Models: Enhancing Regulatory Effectiveness
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE PES Innovative Smart Grid Technologies - Asia (ISGT Asia)
abstract: Ensuring the reliability and efficiency of electricity distribution networks requires a proactive framework that effectively manages and mitigates the risks associated with grid component failures. The Common Network Assets Methodology (CNAIM), widely used for regulation in the United Kingdom, stands as a state-of-the-art example of integrating Component Risk Models in incentive regulation. However, its limitations become apparent when it comes to accurately reflecting the impact of digital applications, such as dynamic line rating. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel approach by incorporating the impact of digitalisation into CNAIM’s risk calculation, utilizing Digitalisation Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) specifically designed for Distribution Network Operators (DNOs). This offers a promising pathway for further advancements in accurately representing asset risks and the impacts of digital applications. Embracing this comprehensive consideration, along with a risk-based approach to managing distribution grid assets, becomes fundamental in navigating the challenges faced by DNOs both in the present and the future.
